definitions.explanation: A container with a vacuum-insulated interior that keeps beverages hot or cold. Literally 'magic bottle.'

examples.japanese: {魔法瓶|まほうびん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦お{茶|ちゃ}→お茶：00576_ocha⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{入|い}れる→入れる：01098_ireru⟧。
⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧{魔法瓶|まほうびん}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{六時間|ろくじかん}{温|あたた}かさ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{続|つづ}く→続く：00903_tsuzuku⟧。
examples.english: This thermos keeps things warm for six hours.

examples.japanese: ⟦{冬|ふゆ}→冬：00623_fuyu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ハイキング→ハイキング：03869_haikingu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{魔法瓶|まほうびん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{温|あたた}かい→温かい：13395_atatakai⟧⟦スープ→スープ：00395_suupu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{入|い}れて→入れる：01098_ireru⟧⟦{持|も}っていく→持っていく：27431_motteiku⟧。
examples.english: For winter hikes, I put warm soup in a thermos and bring it along.

notes:
Literally "magic bottle" (⟦{魔法|まほう}→魔法：14640_mahou⟧ + ⟦{瓶|びん}→瓶：01016_bin⟧), named because the vacuum insulation seemed magical when the technology was new.

USAGE:
While {魔法瓶|まほうびん} is the generic term, the brand name サーモス (Thermos) is also widely recognized. In everyday speech, ⟦{水筒|すいとう}→水筒：04299_suitou⟧ (water bottle/canteen) is often used for portable insulated containers, while {魔法瓶|まほうびん} may refer to larger tabletop models as well.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {魔法瓶|まほうびん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{入|い}れる→入れる：01098_ireru⟧: to put in a thermos
- {魔法瓶|まほうびん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{持|も}っていく→持っていく：27431_motteiku⟧: to bring a thermos
- ⟦{保温|ほおん}→保温：17467_hoon⟧{魔法瓶|まほうびん}: heat-retaining thermos
- {魔法瓶|まほうびん}⟦タイプ→タイプ：01534_taipu⟧: thermos-type (describing insulated products)

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{水筒|すいとう}→水筒：04299_suitou⟧: water bottle, canteen
- ⟦{保温|ほおん}→保温：17467_hoon⟧: heat retention
- {保冷|ほれい}: cold retention
- ⟦{真空|しんくう}→真空：04174_shinkuu⟧: vacuum (as in ⟦{真空|しんくう}→真空：04174_shinkuu⟧⟦{断熱|だんねつ}→断熱：06427_dannetsu⟧, vacuum insulation)
